title: A Message, Not a Job: That Your Young One Lives for a Greater Purpose
summary: Many young people choose their field of study and work without a compass, lost between the pressures of this world and anxiety about the future. Help your child connect their worldly ambition to an ultimate, hereafter-oriented purpose: to benefit people, cultivate the earth, and seek the Face of Allah through their work. True success is *itqan* (excellence) and *ikhlas* (sincerity), with a benefit that extends beyond oneself—not merely a degree or wealth.
try_this: This week: Ask your child, «If you could benefit your *ummah* with one thing, what would you choose?» Then help them take one small, practical step toward that dream.
reflection_prompts: What truly excites your child and makes them speak with passion?
How did you connect their ambition to a righteous *niyyah* (intention) this week?
warning_flags: فقدان دافع تام أو انسحاب من المستقبل

review_defects.why: The Arabic consistently addresses the parent of a son (شابك, ابنك), while the English uses gender-neutral terms (young one, child). This changes the intended audience from specifically parents of boys to parents of any child.
The word 'ultimate' is added; the Arabic only says 'an otherworldly purpose' without the intensifier 'ultimate'.
